discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 260531
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
131 AM EDT Mon Oct 26 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Warm and dry conditions persist for much of this week with highs 
  in the 70s and lows around 50.

- There is a chance for light rain near Lake Michigan on
  Thursday with a better chance for more widespread rain early
  next week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 130 AM EDT Mon Oct 26 2026

A weak convergent boundary is noted on radar mosaic and surface obs 
just to our northwest this morning. This front is associated with an 
upper low crossing Hudson Bay and is becoming increasingly diffuse 
as the parent forcing zips east and strong mid/upper ridge holds 
over the Ohio Valley. No rain is expected locally, just a steady 
stream of high clouds given incredibly dry and stable low levels. 
Our area does see a wind shift later today into tonight to NNE and 
eventually east. Will have to keep an eye on fog potential given 
return of Lake Erie contribution but ample high clouds may limit 
development as is occurring now. Highs today still reach low 70s 
ahead of the front and flow veers back to a more southerly direction 
by Tue afternoon so highs on Tue are still around 70 (slightly 
cooler far NE).

S/SW flow and warm/moist air advection ramp up again Tue night 
through Thu as another front take aims at the region. A more 
southward track of the parent trough and a much better prefrontal 
LLJ/theta-e surge suggest at least some chances for rain on Thu. The 
trough is still well to the north though and local areas remain 
relatively dry and stable. Best chances for some light rain will be 
in our far NW Thu afternoon. Latest NBM even throws in a chance for 
thunder in our NW but not expecting anything significant and areas 
along/south of US-24 likely remain dry. Highs do climb near 80 on 
Thu, which is the record (set in 2024).

Upper ridge finally breaks down this weekend with potential for a 
southern stream trough to tap into better moisture and bring our 
best chances for rain in a while. Still a ton of spread regarding 
the timing and evolution though. Halloween still looks mostly dry 
but NBM is maintaining some slight chance PoPs. Better chances 
arrive Sunday into Monday but confidence on timing and amounts 
couldn't be much lower.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 130 AM EDT Mon Oct 26 2026

A large scale upper trough working across south central Canada
is allowing a weak cold front to sag south across the Great
Lakes region. This front is expected to be shallow in nature as
far south as northern Indiana, with more aggressive southern 
push limited by the fact the forcing with the upper wave will 
already be waning later this morning. This front is expected to 
lose its integrity today but should provide a weak northerly sfc
wind component at KSBN this afternoon. A narrow zone of post-
frontal MVFR low clouds may accompany this front, but the 
greater potential of this appears to be across west central 
Lower MI into northeast Illinois. VFR conditions should hold 
through this period, with fog potential looking significantly 
lower than previous few nights.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

spc.text:
SPC AC 260519

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1219 AM CDT Mon Oct 26 2026

   Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorm are not expected Monday.

   ... Synopsis ...

   Broad upper troughing will remain in place across the western
   contiguous US today. Within this regime, a shortwave trough over the
   southern and central High Plains will eject northeastward toward the
   upper Mississippi Valley, accompanied by a weak surface low. A
   trailing cold front will extend southwestward from this low across
   the central Plains into the southern High Plains, with a lee trough
   sharpening along its western flank. Farther west, an upper cyclone
   will deepen as it digs southeastward across the northern Great Basin
   and Intermountain West. 


   ... Southern High Plains into the Midwest ...

   Surface dewpoints in the mid 50Fs to near 60 F will remain in place
   ahead of the slow-moving baroclinic zone/surface boundary today.
   Diurnal heating of this modestly moist boundary layer will yield
   weak destabilization from southern and eastern New Mexico and Far
   West Texas northeastward into the Texas/Oklahoma Panhandles and
   southwest Kansas. Isolated thunderstorms may develop along the front
   and lee trough during the late afternoon and evening, with
   additional development probable farther northeast into the Midwest
   overnight as low-level warm air advection strengthens. 

   Buoyancy will be somewhat greater across southern New Mexico and Far
   West Texas, where a few stronger cores could produce hail or gusty
   winds. Even there, modest deep-layer shear and warm/warming midlevel
   temperatures in the wake of the departing midlevel trough should
   limit updraft intensity and organization. Thus, severe probabilities
   are currently not warranted. 


   ... Idaho and surrounding areas ...

   Cooling midlevel temperatures and large-scale ascent accompanying
   the digging upper cyclone will steepen lapse rates across Idaho and
   adjacent areas during the afternoon. Despite limited moisture,
   sufficient buoyancy may materialize to support isolated low-topped
   thunderstorms during the afternoon and into the evening. Strong flow
   aloft could support locally gusty winds, and hail could accompany
   stronger thunderstorm cores. The cool surface temperatures and
   limited instability should limit any severe threat.

   ..Marsh/Thornton.. 10/26/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 260512

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1212 AM CDT Mon Oct 26 2026

   Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are unlikely Tuesday.

   ...Synopsis...

   A series of upper shortwave troughs will move across the northern
   Plains and Upper Midwest, as well as the southern Plains to the
   Mid-MS Valley on Tuesday. Boundary layer moisture will remain
   modest, with dewpoints generally in the 50s across the Plains and
   Midwest, while 60s dewpoints remain confined to central/south TX.
   Warmer midlevel temperatures will preclude much destabilization from
   the Mid/Lower MO Valley into the Upper Midwest. This will largely
   limit thunderstorm activity and negate severe thunderstorm potential
   despite stronger southwesterly flow aloft. Further south across TX,
   isolated thunderstorms are more likely where weak destabilization
   will occur amid marginally better moisture and stronger heating.
   However, vertical shear will remain modest as the region is
   displaced to the south of stronger flow across the north-central
   U.S. Furthermore, large-scale ascent will be nebulous within a broad
   low-level warm advection regime. Overall, severe thunderstorm
   potential appears low for Tuesday.

   ..Leitman.. 10/26/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 260616

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0116 AM CDT Mon Oct 26 2026

   Valid 281200Z - 291200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorm potential appears low on Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...

   A low-amplitude west/southwesterly upper-level flow regime will
   overspread much of the CONUS on Wednesday. Stronger westerlies will
   extend from the Pacific Northwest to the Great Lakes, weakening with
   southward extent. Surface high pressure will be focused over the
   eastern U.S., while modest surface troughing extends from the Upper
   Midwest to the southern High Plains. South/southwesterly low-level
   flow will transport modest boundary layer moisture northward across
   portions of the southern/central Plains and into the Upper MS
   Valley. Isolated thunderstorm activity will be possible within this
   plume of modest moisture and weak destabilization. Any stronger
   instability is forecast to be across the southern Plains,
   particularly TX, where deeper moisture will be in place (compared to
   further north). However, weak vertical shear and a lack of focused
   ascent will limit severe potential. Further north across the Upper
   Midwest, instability will be weaker given a cooler and less moist
   airmass, precluding severe potential, despite stronger deep-layer
   west/southwesterly flow.

   ..Leitman.. 10/26/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
